_comment: ⭐ THE FIRST NPC IN THE GAME (content-zone-design-guide.md §2.0): the player's mother, at the homestead the road to Reinhard's farm starts from. Standing talkable-NPC shape copied field for field from miller.json — faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it), collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) and deliberately NOT Action(2) so no aura on either side can target it, mask 16 = Border only, role creature + speed 0 (D4), xpFactor 0 to keep it off the nameplate path, aggroRadius 1.0 required-but-inert since interaction.range 2.0 sizes the one sensor. ⚑ QUESTS: offers and turns in `dinner-for-the-family`, the game's opening arc — she sends the player to her husband Hendrik for meat and her brother-in-law Benjamin for beets, and each errand is where one of the three starting skills is taught. ⭐ SHE TEACHES FirstAid ON THE TURN-IN ROW rather than from a `Teach me something.` node: it is the dinner's reward, the-lost-lamp/Lantern shape, so the mother patches you up after your first hunt instead of drilling you beforehand. ⚑ FirstAid also has two village teachers (Hermit, VillageHealer @L2) — the two-teacher precedent is Torch's; hers is the EARLIEST and free, which is the point. ⭐ HER COMPLETED GREETING IS THE HANDOFF: a `quest_at_stage completed` node sitting ABOVE the unconditional root (L3 — conditional nodes must outrank the greeting) points the player down the road to Reinhard. ⛑ entityType VillageHealer is a DELIBERATE REUSE and placeholder art. ⚑ TEXT HAS A VOICE, by PO ask 2026-09-23 — the opening family is the one exception to the plain-text pass (PO 2026-08-02): she is warm, and worried about the player leaving home. The PLAYER'S rows stay on the plain conventions ('Do you have a task for me?', 'Teach me something.', a teach row names its skill) so the panel reads the same as everywhere else. ⚑ UNPLACED: the PO places the spawn in the editor. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
name: Eliza

lines: You ate everything. Good. You'll need it.
Reinhard's farm is east, down the road. He's a fair man, and he'll give you work.
Stay on the road, and come home when you can. I mean that.
There you are. Come here, let me look at you.
Taller than your father already. I don't know when that happened.

options.text: Do you have a task for me?

lines: One last dinner at home before you go. I want to do this properly.
Your father is out hunting down south by the lake. Help him find his game.
And your uncle Benjamin has beets. Six. Don't let him talk your ear off.
Come back to me when you have both. Then we eat.

grants.line: Thank you. Go on, before I change my mind about letting you out of the house.

options.text: I have the meat and the beets.

grants.line: Look at that. Sit, sit. It's nearly ready.
Before you go anywhere: I'll teach you First Aid. You won't have me out there to patch you up.
Now eat. Slowly. I want to remember this.
